links.targetTitle: Rebate eligibility is tied to custody: all other-Agent token
Osero's Pioneer Incentive Pool is not a segregated account —

title: Osero must keep all other Agents' tokens in its SubProxy account, making the rebate base observable
content:
A.6.1.1.7.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.1 is the first step of the Upkeep Rebate Routine Protocol and reads simply: "Osero keeps all tokens of other Agents it holds in its SubProxy account."

Read alone it is a housekeeping rule. Read as step one of the rebate process it is the precondition for everything after it. The rebate is computed from holdings of other Prime Agents' tokens; unless those holdings sit in one address the Artifact names, the figure Osero reports cannot be independently reconstructed.

The SubProxy account is specified in the Agent Creation parameters, so the address is already public in the Artifact. Concentrating the rebate-eligible assets there means Operational GovOps can perform its verification (A.6.1.1.7.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.3) against onchain state rather than against a statement from Osero.

The rule is absolute — "all tokens of other Agents" — which closes the obvious gap. A partial custody requirement would let an Agent hold some peer tokens elsewhere and choose which to disclose; requiring all of them in one place makes both over-claiming and selective reporting visible.
description: A single named custody location turns the rebate from a self-reported holdings figure into something a reviewer can check onchain against a known address.
